items.title: How ECI's dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
items.shows: From the Commission's own suspect-list summaries, it shows software flagged about 1.31 crore West Bengal and 2.35 crore Madhya Pradesh electors for 'logical discrepancies' with no written protocol for resolving them.

items.title: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
items.shows: It uses official records and interviews with election officials to argue that the West Bengal notices were produced in bulk by central software, and that registration officers did not review them one by one as the Commission told the Court.

items.title: How EC Has Quietly Changed Form 6 During SIR, Evading Parliament
items.shows: It traces how the Commission changed Form 6 in each round of the SIR, first adding a declaration in Bihar and later altering the online form itself, with no amendment to the rules. Former Commission officials it quotes say only the government can change the form, under the oversight of Parliament.

items.title: Delhi SIR: With More Than Half the Voters in India's Capital Either Purged or on ECI's Doubtful List, VIPs Get a Pass and the Poorest Pay
items.authors: Shubhangi Derhgawen, Dikshya Koirala, Sumedha Mittal
items.shows: From booth-wise lists of names left off and ground reporting, it finds 79.2 lakh of Delhi's 1.45 crore electors were left off the draft or sent a notice, with the heaviest losses among the poorest, including residents of demolished settlements.

items.title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
items.shows: From internal notes and letters of November 2025 to August 2026, it shows that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times to SIR decisions, including the Form 6 change, centralised control of the roll software and the West Bengal appeals.

items.title: 'Illegal, unauthorised': Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
items.shows: It is a companion piece, and it shows how a new declaration section was added to Form 6 against the written advice of two Commissioners, who said it needed an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules.

items.title: No VIP Left Behind: ECI’s Drive to Guarantee a Spot For Them on the Final Voter Roll
items.authors: Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen, Sumedha Mittal, Dikshya Koirala
items.shows: It reports that the Delhi revision gave people the Commission treated as VIPs a separate route onto the roll, through a 'Mark VIP' module in the booth-level officers' app, WhatsApp groups and orders. Ordinary electors with notices were sent to queues and hearings.

items.title: The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll
items.shows: It sets the 71.38 lakh Form 6 applications the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published against the 84.3 lakh electors added to the final roll. It traces the gap to 16.18 lakh applications taken before the draft, whose names and details were never published as the rules require.

items.title: UP CEO Confirms: 16.18 Lakh Applications for Addition Accepted Before Draft Roll. Falsely Claims Details Were Hidden on ECI’s Instructions
items.shows: It follows the earlier report on 16.18 lakh additions in Uttar Pradesh. The state's Chief Electoral Officer confirmed the Form 6 applications were taken before the draft roll and said their details were withheld on the Commission's instructions, and the report sets that against Commission instructions requiring applications after the draft and public details.

items.title: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 85,854 Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen
items.shows: From the more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 objections the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published, it finds that the roll software generated 85,854 deletion forms giving no reason, carrying the officers' digital signatures. It also counts 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals accepted after the legal deadline.

items.title: Delhi SIR: ECI Forcing BLOs to Sign Off on Voters Without Verification
items.shows: It reports that booth-level officers in Delhi were told over WhatsApp to clear electors flagged for 'logical discrepancies' by signing a new 'certificate' form. Under this route the flagged cases are closed with no documents and no hearing.

items.title: UP CEO Admits ECI Auto-generated 85,000+ Voter Deletion Forms Without a Reason, Confirms Mass Deletion Attempts Against Muslims
items.authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar (edited by Nitin Sethi)
items.shows: It is a follow-up to the Collective's investigation of 9 October 2026 into the 85,854 Form 7s that the Commission's software ERONET produced in Uttar Pradesh with no reason for deletion. It reports that the state's Chief Electoral Officer answered on X within minutes, calling the report false, and that evening called it misleading in a recorded video, in which he did not dispute the count or explain why the reasons were missing. It quotes him putting the names targeted by bulk Form 7s at about 4,700 among 13.39 crore electors, and reports that the Commission capped the number of deletion objections one person may file.

items.title: Amit Shah and ECI claim SIR Was to Catch ‘Infiltrators’. Commission Has no Record of Them
items.authors: Ayushi Kar (edited by Mayank Aggarwal, visual by Nitin Sethi)
items.shows: From its RTI applications and its reporting on the Commission's software, the Collective finds that the SIR gave officers no way to record anyone as a foreigner. The Commission passed its questions on cases referred under the Citizenship Act to Bihar alone. The Bihar replies it reproduces answer No to whether any list was referred and give the constituency's names left off by reason, with no category for people who are not citizens. It sets this beside the Home Minister's statement that the Leader of the Opposition was protecting infiltrators.

items.title: Inside India’s electoral overhaul that removed 130mn voters
items.shows: It reports from Hyderabad, where the revision was in its last phase, on residents of a Muslim neighbourhood whose names were left off the draft roll, one of whom said 17 members of his family and 13 neighbours were left off, his family as permanently shifted. It sets out critics' view that the revision wrongly took eligible voters off the rolls, many of them Muslim, and may have helped the Prime Minister's party, and notes that protesters have produced no evidence that it changed any result. It quotes a former election commissioner calling the exercise aggressive, ambitious and abrupt, and the Commission's reply that its decisions follow standard administrative practice and that it has directed officials to restore eligible voters left off in error. The 130 million in its headline are names left off the drafts.

items.title: The ECI Software Deleted 5.38 Lakh Bengal Voters With Auto-Generated Rejections Without Citing a Reason
items.shows: It reads the Form 10 registers published with West Bengal's final roll for 284 of the 294 constituencies and finds 5,23,998 names deleted on Form 7s that give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank. It quotes the Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 that the state's Form 7 figure included forms the Commission's software generated when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing, and puts those at 5,38,320 of the state's 5.46 lakh Form 7 deletions. It breaks the deletions down by district and by the party that won each seat, and sets them against the 2026 margins.

items.title: Audit finds Bengal-specific access curbs in ECINET code
items.shows: It reports a review of ECINET's publicly served code by Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found a rule that can bar registration officers in West Bengal from the page that shows each enumeration form with its documents and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard, and found no such rule for any other state. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, so it cannot say whether the rule was used or enforced on the server, and the paper says it could not verify the review. The Commission did not answer the paper's questions.

items.title: On ECINet platform, access for States can be switched off and on centrally: report
items.shows: It reports another finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. The portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers with a disable button on each, and the code carries a message for States where viewing enumeration form details is not enabled. The review read only code the site serves before login, and the report does not say who can use either control or whether either was used.

items.title: ECINET Audit Finds State-Level Access Could be Restricted by Election Commission, VIP Tags for Voters
items.shows: It is Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's publicly served code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, reported in three findings. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule, it reports code showing a gold VIP symbol against some voters on officials' screens and a button that downloads a list of these voters by constituency. The review cannot say whether any feature was used, and the criteria for marking a voter are not known.

items.title: The Election Commission Filed 16 Lakh Appeals Against Included Bengal Voters Over Just 3 Days as the Rolls Froze
items.shows: The appeal records for West Bengal, collected by the Civic Research Group and checked by The Wire, show the Commission appealed against 16,08,175 of the 32,53,401 voters the judicial officers had cleared, or 49.4%. In an earlier extract of 13,95,794 appeal IDs, 99.3% carry a timestamp of 5, 6 or 8 April, and more than 12 lakh carry 5 April. The Commission told the Supreme Court in September that it had filed 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion.

items.title: Uttarakhand ERO refused BJP worker’s bulk Form 7 objections. After ECI complaint, 5,359 were accepted
items.shows: It follows the Form 7 objections in Kichha, Uttarakhand, from the Chief Electoral Officer's Form 10 data to the final roll of 3 October. Of 4,390 names on the draft that are missing from the final roll, about 670 had an objection against them and 3,720 had none and were deleted for logical discrepancies. One BJP booth level agent filed 5,359 of the 6,884 objections accepted, and 504 of his carry an acceptance date a day after claims closed. A second part meets electors deleted after his objections whose notices gave other reasons.

items.title: यूपी में एसआईआर की जिन गड़बड़ियों को लेकर चुनाव आयोग है निशाने पर
items.shows: It sets out what is known of the Pilibhit Sadar case, from the Congress's allegation of 13,150 changed names to the Chief Electoral Officer's note of 22 October on 13,779 Form 8 entries with no records behind them. BBC Hindi checked rolls itself and found two electors at one polling station in Bareilly each entered under two EPIC numbers, and one elector in Pilibhit Sadar entered under three. It could not reach Pilibhit's Deputy District Election Officer for comment. It also recounts the Samajwadi Party's complaint of duplicates and the Chief Electoral Officer's instruction of 19 October to delete them through Form 7.

items.title: 'Dear Bengal Poll Chief, How Many Voters Have ECI Staff Tried to Delete?' Asks Jawhar Sircar
items.shows: It reports the nine questions that Jawhar Sircar, a former Rajya Sabha member and former Secretary to the Government of India, put in a letter to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer, Neelam Meena. He asks how many applications election officers filed before the tribunals to delete names, under what authority and how many names were deleted, which notification introduced 'logical discrepancies' and how many electors they affected, whether ECINET can stop registration officers from seeing enumeration forms and the hearing dashboard, and whether every elector left off is covered by the special drive. The report sets the questions beside its own earlier figures on the appeals and the discrepancy flags.

items.title: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
items.shows: It counts 61,059 Form 7 applications in Karnataka filed by registration officers themselves, none giving a reason, from the Commission's Form 10 records, and finds that more than 60,800 of them came after claims closed on 23 September. Officers said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices could not be reached. Every elector the paper checked had already been deleted, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more objections than voters or third parties did.

items.title: On last day of SIR camps in Delhi, BLOs wait, go door to door
items.shows: It visits the special enrolment camps in Chilla, New Moti Bagh and Sarai Kale Khan on their last day, where booth level officers received few or no Form 6 applications and spent the day on notices and door to door visits. It sets this against about 47.5 lakh electors left off Delhi's draft of 31 August and about 4.7 lakh Form 6 applications so far, and follows a first time applicant held up at the declaration about his parents' entry in the last intensive revision.

items.title: Press Note: Special Intensive Revision - Phase III (No. ECI/PN/086/2026)
items.shows: It is the Commission's own announcement of the third phase in 16 states and 3 union territories, with its count of booth level officers and agents and its summary of the first two phases.

items.title: 'Differing views' part of 'decision-making', says EC, does not address concerns two ECs red-flagged
items.shows: It reports the Election Commission's first response to the investigation. The Commission calls the 14 notes suggestions and says every decision was unanimous, and the paper sets out what the response does not address.

items.title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/120/2026): decisions of the meeting of the Commission held on 26.09.2026
items.shows: It is the Commission's own record of the nine decisions of its full meeting of 26 September 2026. Among them are home visits by booth level officers in place of hearings for electors sent a notice, a review of ECINET by a committee with an outside expert, and later deadlines for claims in Delhi and Maharashtra. It also says the SIR is complete in 20 states and union territories and orders a drive to enrol those left out.

items.title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/121/2026)
items.shows: It records a Commission meeting attended by all three Commissioners that extended the SIR in Andhra Pradesh (claims and notices to 10 October, final roll on 16 October) and moved Meghalaya's final roll to 26 October 2026.

items.title: Special drive in States/UTs after completion of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) – reg. (Letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II))
items.shows: It is the Commission's letter to all Chief Electoral Officers ordering a drive to enrol left-out and young electors. Booth-level officers are to compare the current roll with the pre-SIR roll, list everyone missing, visit each house within about a month, help eligible people fill Form 6 and share the lists with party agents.

items.title: SIR Row: Seven fake claims made on electoral roll by Congress and opposition examined and debunked
items.shows: Organiser sets out the BJP's account of the revision, from a video the party posted on 25 October 2026 in answer to seven allegations by the INDIA bloc. By the BJP's account, the 13 crore names were only flagged in the drafts as dead, shifted, absent or duplicate, Form 6 itself is unchanged and the Supreme Court upheld the declaration added to it, registration officers in each state still manage the rolls, and about 2.37 crore young electors have been added since the revision began. The BJP also says the three Election Commissioners decide together, lists five safeguards against fraud and defends the 2023 law on appointing them. Organiser adds that these figures need checking against official records. On 12 October 2026 the Supreme Court said it had neither approved nor disapproved the modified Form 6, as Bar and Bench reported. In its affidavit of 26 October 2026 the Commission told the Supreme Court that Form 6 had not been amended and that the declaration is a separate document, as Bar and Bench reported.

items.title: 'SIR Risks Disenfranchising Millions of Legitimate Citizens Over Lack of Documents': Lokniti-CSDS Survey
items.shows: It reports a Lokniti-CSDS survey across Delhi and five states. 52% of respondents had no birth certificate and 41% no domicile certificate, with sharp gaps between states.

items.title: Bihar SIR: Latest ECI data raises more questions over higher deletions among women
items.authors: Areena Arora, Srinivasan Ramani, Vignesh Radhakrishnan
items.shows: Using the list of about 65 lakh Bihar electors left off the draft, which the Supreme Court made the Commission publish, it shows women far outnumbered men among those marked 'permanently shifted', most of all below age 40.

items.title: More men die in Bihar, but more women vanish from its voter rolls
items.shows: It sets the Commission's counts of names left off by reason and sex against state death records and finds about 7.6 lakh more women than men left off, including more women entered as dead, although more men die.

items.title: Why exclusion of women voters in Bihar should worry Nitish Kumar
items.shows: It compares Bihar's January 2025 roll with the final SIR roll and finds women were close to 59% of the fall in the roll and the gender ratio of the roll fell in 230 of 243 seats.

items.title: Bihar 2025: In 11 Seats, SIR Deletions Outnumbered Victory Margins
items.shows: It finds 11 Bihar seats where the names left off or deleted exceeded the winning margin, separates the 47 lakh net fall from the 3.66 lakh deleted after the draft, and says the landslide made the numbers moot statewide.

items.title: What Election Commission data says about 'vote chori' in the Bihar elections
items.shows: It checks booth-level results in villages where many names were left off or deleted, the 28 close contests and late additions to the roll, and finds no anomaly that stands out. The NDA won exactly half the close contests.

items.title: After SIR, 13.4% deletions in Gujarat electoral rolls
items.authors: Abhishek Jha, Maulik Pathak, Harsh Yadav
items.shows: It reads Gujarat's final roll of 4.40 crore against the pre-SIR roll, a net fall of 13.4 per cent. The largest falls were in Surat, Ahmedabad and Vadodara and the smallest in the tribal districts of Dang, Chhota Udepur and Narmada.

items.title: Bengal Has 62 Lakh 'Under Adjudication' Electors. Here's Why That Number Is Significant.
items.shows: It sets West Bengal's final roll against the National Commission on Population's projection of adults for 2026 and finds a gap of about 65.7 lakh, with electors at about 91.5% of projected adults.

items.title: More women deleted from rolls in most States after SIR
items.shows: It compares women per 1,000 men on the 2024 Lok Sabha rolls and the final SIR rolls across the second-phase states and finds the ratio fell in every major state except Tamil Nadu.

items.title: Over 61 Lakh Women Dropped from Bengal Voter Rolls, Data Show Stark Gender Bias in SIR
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty, Bhanupriya Rao, Souptik Halder
items.shows: From the Commission's lists, it finds roughly three in five electors left off, deleted or held under adjudication on West Bengal's roll were women, most heavily in Muslim-majority, Scheduled Tribe and Matua seats.

items.title: 4 tests, 1 question: Did SIR shape Bengal outcome?
items.shows: It runs four tests of the names West Bengal left off or deleted against the 2026 margins and swings. The net count exceeded the BJP's margin in 82 seats but exceeded the swing in margin in only 12 flipped seats, and the names held for adjudication passed the two tests in 49 and 14 seats.

items.title: SIR redraws Bengal’s margins of power
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty, Souptik Halder
items.shows: It finds the names left off or deleted in West Bengal's revision outnumbered the winning margin in 161 of 293 Assembly seats, and still did so in 124 seats once deaths are left out.

items.title: SIR exclusions in West Bengal were connected to the AITC lead and Muslim population
items.shows: Using the Sabar Institute's data on names left off or deleted, it reports that those names exceeded the margin in 102 of the BJP's 207 seats and, by its own summary, a regression in which they rose with how hard a seat was for the BJP to win.

items.title: Data analysis: How SIR deletions shaped BJP’s landslide in Bengal
items.shows: It sets each West Bengal seat's roll shrinkage against the change in the BJP and TMC margin from 2021 to 2026, and finds each point of shrinkage went with a shift of about 0.38 points toward the BJP. The same test on Bihar finds no such pattern, and the authors describe the Bengal result as an association.

items.title: Comprehensive Analysis of ASDD Deletions in Uttarakhand under the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls, 2026
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: It finds at least 8,07,410 names on Uttarakhand's ASDD lists, 52.0% of them women and 57.7% recorded as permanently shifted, more than the 2022 winning margin in 45 of 70 seats.

items.title: Fact Sheet on Voter Deletion Patterns in the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR), 2025–26
items.shows: Reading 91 lakh elector records, it finds women were 53.6% of the 58 lakh names left off the draft in December 2025 and that in Nandigram, where Muslims are about a quarter of the population, they were 95% of the names deleted from the supplementary lists.

items.title: Preliminary Report on SIR Meghalaya : State-wide analysis of all 60 Assembly Constituencies
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: It finds 1,80,402 names on Meghalaya's ASDD lists, 8.32% of the draft roll, with death the largest recorded reason at 45.2% and the count above the 2023 winning margin in 32 of 60 seats.

items.title: Bengaluru to Lucknow, why urban centres are seeing high electoral roll deletions during SIR
items.shows: It compares the district with the highest share of names left off in several states, which are the Bengaluru districts in Karnataka (43 to 49 per cent), Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Surat in Gujarat, Chennai in Tamil Nadu, Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, Gurugram and Hyderabad. A former Chief Election Commissioner and a former Election Commissioner put the pattern down to migration, and the second says that deleting electors for failing to map to the 2002-03 roll would be unfair.

items.title: SIR draft rolls see over 13 crore deletions so far, Delhi leads with 33% left out
items.shows: It tallies the names left off the draft rolls across the states revised so far, over 13 crore, with Delhi the highest at about a third of its roll.

items.title: SIR Draft Rolls Show Highest Voter Deletions in States Where Elections Were Held in Last 3 Years
items.shows: It tabulates the phase 3 draft rolls, 6.15 crore names left off across 17 states and UTs. The five states with the most names left off (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh) all held Assembly elections between 2023 and 2025, and the lowest shares were in Mizoram, Odisha, Manipur, Meghalaya and Sikkim.

items.title: SIR Delhi 2026: The Excluded Roll and the 2025 Verdict
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: Across all 14,947 polling parts it counts 47,56,722 uncollectable enumeration forms, 32.8% of Delhi's electorate, more than the 2025 winning margin in 68 of 70 seats.

items.title: SIR: Glaring oddities in Maharashtra’s deletion patterns
items.shows: It finds that shifted or absent made up 75% to 96.5% of the names left off in 85 Maharashtra constituencies, and that neighbouring seats in Pune used the two reasons very differently. It estimates that the draft roll falls about 1.92 crore short of the projected adult population.

items.title: SIR: Deletions go up in Phase 3 with more marked as ‘Shifted’ or ‘Absent’
items.shows: It finds that the 17 phase 3 states and territories with draft rolls left off 6.15 crore names, 17.1%, against 12.3% in the first two phases, with a larger share marked shifted or absent. It also finds that the full lists of names left off for Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana mark no one as 'Others', though the Chief Electoral Officers' press notes put 9.73 lakh names left off in phase 3 under that reason.

items.title: In seat Kejriwal lost by thin margin, nearly 40% names added before 2025 polls missing in SIR draft
items.shows: It follows the New Delhi seat, which had 1,08,788 electors at the 2025 election and lost 37,315 names in the SIR draft. It finds that 560 of the 1,430 voters added in January 2025, about four in ten, are missing from the draft.

items.title: Explainer: Why fewer voters were deleted in Odisha compared to several other states
items.shows: It sets Odisha's net fall of 17.67 lakh (about 5.3 per cent) from the pre-SIR roll to the final roll of 21 September against other states. It gives a 94 per cent return of enumeration forms, few duplicates and mostly seasonal migration as the reasons, and explains how an elector left off or deleted can appeal or reapply.

items.title: SIR Manipur 2026: Preliminary Report on Electoral Roll Deletions
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: Of the 1,58,677 names left off the draft in Manipur, the 20 hill seats account for 66.4% and women for 55.96%, and women are the majority of those left off in all 60 seats.

items.title: Analysis and Explainer on How the SIR Excluded Voters at Scale
items.shows: It draws on official figures for names left off and an RTI reply on West Bengal appeals. Delhi's draft excluded 32.78% of electors, 91.13% of the decided West Bengal appeals restored the elector, and the public still cannot check the rolls.

items.title: SIR: Telangana may witness net deletion of 70 lakh names or more from electoral rolls
items.shows: It reports that Telangana's draft of 17 August left off more than 73 lakh electors while fresh enrolment applications stayed under 5 lakh, so the net fall may reach 70 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer's figures show more than 10.2 lakh claims and objections received by 7 October.

items.title: The Link Between TCS, SIR’s Digital Stack, and the Noel Tata-N. Chandrasekaran Tussle
items.shows: It argues that ERONET and ECINET, the roll software Tata Consultancy Services built for the Commission, moved control of the roll away from the registration officers the law names, citing Goa's 97 electors and Uttar Pradesh's Form 7s. It says the links it draws to the Tata group prove no wrongdoing.

items.title: Amid elector apathy, EC extends Maharashtra SIR deadline yet again till October 26
items.shows: It gives the reasons behind Maharashtra's 2.07 crore names left off the draft (7.68 million shifted, 7.55 million absent, 3.48 million dead, 1.76 million duplicates). By 12 October only 8.33 lakh applications and 25,661 Form 7 objections had come in, and 1.22 crore electors on the draft were flagged as unmapped or discrepant.

items.title: Muslims disproportionately flagged in Delhi SIR
items.shows: The Hindu read Delhi's draft roll of 97.54 lakh electors, matched it to the lists of the 33.12 lakh sent notices (13.79 lakh unmapped with the last SIR and 19.33 lakh for logical discrepancies), and guessed each elector's religion from their name and their relative's name. On that guess, Muslims were 13.6% of the draft roll, 7.6% of the unmapped and 20.3% of those flagged for logical discrepancies, and 30% of those flagged for the five reasons that turn on family size, such as six or more electors naming the same parent. The paper reports that ERONET, the Commission's software, decided who was flagged, that no SIR order mentioned notices for discrepancies before the Commission's direction of 14 May 2026, which still did not set out the reasons, and that the Commission had not answered its questions.

items.title: An entitled generation and an Opposition that protests too much
items.shows: It argues that the gap between the final rolls and the adult population mostly reflects adults who do not register, which he puts at 8.5 per cent of adults from the young missing from the 2024 roll. On that benchmark he estimates about 70 lakh eligible people kept off the rolls of Bihar and eight phase II states, and about 50 lakh in West Bengal alone. He criticises the haste of the revision and the new Form 6 declaration, and asks the Commission to publish deletions by reason, state and booth.

items.title: Much Ado About (Almost) Nothing
items.shows: It is the longer version of his column. It sets out his estimate of adults, his benchmark of 8.5 per cent of adults not registering, a clean roll for each of nine states with final rolls, and sections on Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Assam. He puts the eligible people kept off the rolls at about 70 lakh, with a range of 10 lakh to 1.3 crore, and states which of his figures are his own calculations.

items.title: Let’s not be in denial — disenfranchisement in real
items.shows: It is a reply to Surjit Bhalla that sets the final rolls of nine states against the Technical Group's projected adults for 2026 and finds the rolls about 7 crore, or almost 12 per cent, short, with Uttar Pradesh 2.8 crore short. The authors extend the rate to about 12 crore missing voters nationally, and to about 14 crore on another analyst's estimate of the final rolls, and they say the gap includes adults who were never enrolled. They dispute Bhalla's allowance for young adults who do not register. The print edition carries a table by state.

items.title: Long & short of SIR: What happens when exclusion is prioritised over inclusion
items.shows: This is Drèze's follow-up to the column he wrote with Yogendra Yadav in The Indian Express. He sets the rolls of the major states against the Technical Group's projected adults for 2026 and finds them at 99 per cent before the revision and 85 per cent in the draft lists, and the twelve states with final lists at 97, 86 and 88 per cent. He argues that the rolls before the revision already missed many adults, perhaps up to 10 per cent on what he calls patchy evidence, and that dead, shifted and duplicate names hid the gap. Ground reports suggest most deletions of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors were legitimate, he writes. In his account the gap stayed because the second stage demanded documents from electors who were unmapped or had logical discrepancies, when large-scale use of Form 6 could have enrolled the adults who were missing. Assam and Himachal Pradesh are left out of his table.

items.title: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
items.shows: From appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group, it counts the Election Commission's appeals before West Bengal's SIR tribunals against voters whom judicial officers had found eligible, 14,75,887 of 30,00,545 by 17 October, set out by district and seat, by the minority share of each seat and by the 2026 result, with how few appeals the tribunals had decided.

items.title: SIR: Over 76,000 applications seeking inclusion rejected; net additions far lower than draft stage deletions
items.shows: The Chief Electoral Officer's office gave Karnataka's figures for applications received from 16 June to 23 September. Of 7,87,534 Form 6 applications, 7,08,110 were accepted and 76,176 rejected, against more than 80.62 lakh names left off the draft roll as shifted or absent. Of 58,475 Form 7 applications, 23,926 were accepted. The office had not yet released counts of voters found ineligible.

items.title: Surjit Bhalla: SIR needs reform. But let’s go by numbers, not protestors’ slogans
items.shows: It replies to Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav. For the nine states with final rolls, it takes the figures of 59.9 crore adults and 52.8 crore names, allows for 5.2 crore young people who were not registered in 2024 and 1.5% of adults for older people who never registered, and puts the eligible people wrongly left off at about 1 crore. It also lists what the Commission has not published, including a national roll after the revision and deletions by reason, state and booth.

items.title: Karnataka’s most backward districts see low applications for inclusion after SIR draft deletions
items.shows: The paper sets district figures from Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer for Kalaburagi, Mysuru, Raichur and Ballari, where more than 18% of the electorate was left off the draft roll, against the Form 6 applications received by 23 September. Mysuru received 35,447 against more than 5.57 lakh left off. The office has not released the age of applicants, so first-time voters cannot be told apart from those seeking to return.

items.title: 90% of 33 lakh SIR cases ‘resolved’ or ‘parked for final roll’ in Delhi
items.shows: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office said on 23 October that about 29.5 lakh of the nearly 33 lakh notice cases, 13.79 lakh unmapped and 19.33 lakh flagged for logical discrepancies, had been resolved or parked for the final roll. It did not say how many were rejected. The report also gives the Form 6 count since the draft roll, 2,50,754, and Maharashtra's proposal to change Form 6 for voters seeking to return.

items.title: Irregularities in Voter Lists Like Pilibhit Could Alter UP's Electoral Outcome. Here's Why
items.shows: It sets the Samajwadi Party's list of 100 constituencies where the party alleges duplicate entries against the 2022 Assembly results, and finds that 43 of them were seats the party narrowly won or lost. It counts 124 seats won by fewer than 10,000 votes in 2022 and 53 by fewer than 5,000, beside the 10,470 entries the Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found in Pilibhit, a seat the BJP won by 6,970 votes.

items.title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority
items.shows: It is an economist's counterfactual. Even if every elector deleted after adjudication had voted for the runner-up, the BJP keeps a majority, and only under assumptions the data do not support do the wider counts of names left off or deleted overturn it.

items.title: Power Without Oversight: India’s SIR Judgment and the Unfinished Business of Institutional Design
items.shows: It reads the Supreme Court's SIR judgment against the scholarship on independent electoral bodies and argues that the Commission holds wide power over the rolls without matching accountability.

items.title: How the Invisible Maths of Electoral Roll Revision Altered West Bengal's Election
items.shows: It is an arithmetic test of sensitivity. The gross count of names left off or deleted exceeded the winning margin in 160 seats, and of two no-SIR scenarios one returns the TMC and the other leaves the BJP with a smaller majority. It does not model voter preference.

items.title: Analysis and Explainer on the Software of the SIR That Runs Without Transparency
items.shows: It describes the systems behind the revision (ECINET, the BLO app, ERONET run by TCS since 2023, the mapping and 'logical discrepancy' rules, machine transliteration and duplicate-detection tools) and finds that none has a published specification, threshold or audit. Citing The Reporters' Collective, it gives 1.31 crore electors flagged in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh by the discrepancy rules.

items.title: Supreme Court Upholds Election Commission's Power To Conduct SIR Of Electoral Rolls, Says It Advances Free & Fair Elections
items.shows: It reports the Supreme Court judgment in ADR v. Election Commission holding the SIR within the Commission's powers and its procedure lawful, with a nexus to free and fair elections.

items.title: Bihar SIR Judgement: Three doctrinal gaps
items.shows: It argues that the judgment of 27 May 2026 relies on one half of the 2024 Section 6A ruling, accepts the Commission's reasons for a special revision without a record behind them, and treats the 1995 Lal Babu Hussein judgment on deletions as limited to proceedings against individual electors.

items.title: Supreme Court wants cases of SIR excluded to be decided before next polls. A reality check from Assam
items.shows: It sets the Supreme Court's direction that exclusions be decided before the next polls against Assam's record. About 3 lakh voters were marked 'Doubtful' in a 1997 revision and 93,000 'D' voters remained before the 2026 Assembly election, with cases held up in Foreigners Tribunals and courts.

items.title: Citizen’s Handbook for Filing SIR Voter Deletion Appeals
items.authors: Sarfaraz Ahmed Khan, Tarique Quasimuddin, Darshana Mitra, Sabir Ahamed
items.shows: It is a step-by-step guide to appealing a deletion from West Bengal's roll before the 19 appellate tribunals set up after the Supreme Court's order, with sample appeals for nine common situations.

items.title: Is ECI Correct In Saying Supreme Court Upheld Its New Form 6 Declaration?
items.shows: It examines whether the May 2026 judgment actually considered the declaration the Commission later added to Form 6, as the Commission claimed.

items.title: Powers of the CEC | Day 1: SC seeks ECI’s response on plea
items.shows: It reports the hearing in which the Court issued notice to the Commission and all three Commissioners on petitions alleging the Chief Election Commissioner took decisions alone, and declined to suspend him in the interim. The Chief Justice said no modified Form 6 had been approved by the Court.

items.title: RTI Reveals: In SIR, Purging of ‘Ineligibles’ from the Voter Lists Might be a Bogey
items.shows: The author asked the Election Commission and the Home Ministry under the RTI Act on 10 August 2026 whether the Commission had referred electors it found not to be citizens to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, as the Supreme Court ordered in May 2026 to be done within four weeks. The Commission replied after 50 days that it held none of the information. The Home Ministry transferred its application the same day to the Legislative Department, which sent it on to the Commission, and the Commission then passed the questions to the Home Ministry and to the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar. No reply named the competent authority or gave a number of cases referred.

items.title: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27
items.shows: It reports the bench clarifying that it neither approved nor disapproved the declaration added to Form 6, because it did not exist when the Bihar judgment was given. It sets out the Commission's 26 September claim, the rule-making route under Section 28 of the 1950 Act, and the listing of the challenge for 27 October.

items.title: In India, a Dark Shadow Falls on Its Vaunted Elections
items.shows: It is a lawyer's essay for an international readership on the protests in Delhi on 10 and 12 October 2026 and how the SIR reached them. It argues that the Supreme Court let the revision become a fact on the ground before ruling on it, then upheld it in 2026 and, in the author's view, freed the Commission from having to act proportionately, and that the Commission's independence was never secured in law. It cites the 90% of decided West Bengal appeals that restored the elector and the Indian Express investigation into the two Commissioners' objections.

items.title: SIR Enumeration Form may have violated electoral rules prescribing Form-4 for collecting voter details
items.shows: It sets the enumeration form used in the revision beside Rule 8 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which prescribes Form 4 for collecting electors' details from households, and Rule 25, which says an intensively revised roll is prepared afresh. The form came pre-printed from the 2025 roll and asks for links to the 2002 roll, which Form 4 does not. Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer replied that Form 4 had not been used for a long time and that the format followed the Commission's decision.

items.title: Election Commission’s SIR Damage Control
items.shows: It goes through the measures the Commission announced from 26 September, among them the review of ECINET, the Form 6 declaration in the period outside the SIR, the cap on Form 7 applications of 9 October, and the Special Summary Revision with draft and final rolls in PDF for parties at no cost. It sets them beside the two Election Commissioners' objections and the Cabinet Secretariat's RTI reply, with comments from former Chief Election Commissioner O.P. Rawat, Maj Gen Anil Verma (Retd) of ADR and a co-founder of Voter Adhikar Manch.

items.title: EC says decisions were unanimous but leaves a big question unanswered
items.shows: The Indian Express reads the Election Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 in the Supreme Court against the 14 notes by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi that its investigation reported. By the paper's account, the affidavit says the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken collectively and that a Commissioner's note is not itself a decision, accepts that steps taken by officers on the online Form 6 needed to be corrected, sets out a review of ECINet by a committee with experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru, and says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6. The paper says most of the notes were written after decisions had been taken, and that the affidavit does not say who approved the online change to Form 6 in July, does not mention Joshi's proposal of 29 May for such a committee, and does not say why an order redistributing work in July was issued without the Commission.

items.title: Form 6, voter roll deletions: What Election Commission told the Supreme Court
items.shows: The Indian Express explains what the Election Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 in the Supreme Court means for electors. It sets the affidavit's account of the online Form 6 beside the paper's report of 12 July that a declaration about the last intensive revision had been inserted within the form for every state, and beside the Commission's press note of 26 September. By the paper's account, the Commission decided on 21 October that the online application will be in two parts, so that a new elector can apply through Form 6 without the declaration, which remains a separate requirement where a revision is under way. It also sets out the West Bengal appeals, of which, by the Commission's data, 16.10 lakh were filed against orders of the judicial officers that put names back on the roll, and the affidavit's account of how the Commission takes decisions.

items.title: ECI’s stand that additional declaration is not part of Form 6 comes days after SC said it will examine ‘new’ Form 6
items.shows: Krishnadas Rajagopal reads the Election Commission's affidavit, which says the additional declaration is not part of the statutory Form 6, against the Supreme Court's oral remark of 12 October that the new Form 6 was neither approved nor disapproved in the Bihar judgment and that the Court would examine it. He sets out the petitioners' argument that electors deleted in the revision are made to apply again as fresh voters through Form 6, and the Commission's reply that the declaration let electors give their details in a single document.

items.title: Watch: Bihar SIR: The mystery behind 7 lakh more women elector deletions | Data Point
items.shows: The Hindu's data team sets the gender gap among the names left off Bihar's draft against census migration records and the ages of those left off.

items.title: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण: वोटर लिस्ट की सफ़ाई के वादे पर वोट देने के मूल अधिकार की कब्र खोदने का इंतज़ाम
items.shows: It is a Hindi video version of the Collective's Electoral Roll Project findings. Uploaded 5 March 2026, Pacific time (6 March IST).

items.title: Inside The Election Commission: Investigation Finds ECs Split On Key Issues | Indian Express Special
items.shows: It is the paper's video account of its investigation into the Election Commission. Two Election Commissioners objected on file at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions they said were taken without their knowledge, on deletions, additions, appeals and access to ERONET and ECINET. It also covers the questions added to Form 6, the 97 Goa electors officials could not restore, and the 16 lakh appeals the Commission told the Supreme Court were filed in West Bengal against restored voters.

items.title: Two ECs dissent, questions on legality of SIR process: Constitutional, legal issues & nuances
items.shows: Shekhar Gupta goes through the Indian Express report of the two Election Commissioners' 14 objections, what it shows and what it does not, and the constitutional and legal questions it raises.

items.title: Election Commission Investigation: Ritika Chopra Answers All Your Questions On ECI Investigation
items.shows: The editor who led the paper's investigation into the two Commissioners' objections answers readers' questions on how the software-made 'logical discrepancy' category works, why objections on file by two of three members matter under the law, and what the Commission's reply did and did not deny.

items.title: SIR: 8 Questions, 8 Clear Answers | Election Facts | BJP
items.shows: It is the BJP's own account of the SIR, answering eight questions on topics the party lists as the 13 crore names, Form 6, ECINET, young voters, the role of the Election Commissioners, 'vote chori' and AI. Its description cites the Commission's published material as saying the SIR is meant to include eligible voters and drop ineligible entries, with claims, objections and appeals, and gives Bihar's final roll as about 7.42 crore.

items.title: “13 Crore Voters Deleted?”| The Real SIR Numbers Explained | #SIR | #BJP
items.shows: It is a BJP short on the 13 crore names left off the drafts. Its description splits them, citing the Commission's figures, into absent, shifted or other (9.5 crore, 71%), dead (2.7 crore, 20%) and duplicate (1 crore, 7.6%), argues that, given that split, the 13 crore cannot all be read as eligible voters deleted, and points to the Commission's drive to enrol eligible voters who were left out.

items.title: More SIR Deletions, Bigger BJP Swing? Prannoy Roy DeKodes the Data | DeKoder
items.shows: Prannoy Roy sets the names West Bengal left off or deleted beside the 2026 swing against the TMC and argues that they enlarged it. The episode shows no allowance for other differences between seats, and the other analyses of the same question listed here reach different answers.

items.title: Gyanesh Kumar Row: How did the ECI delete 13 crore voters during the SIR | Insight India
items.shows: It is a conversation with The Hindu's Srinivasan Ramani on how more than 13 crore names came off draft rolls in 30 states and UTs, what the data says about who was left off, and the questions about the exercise's legality.

items.title: Focus on inclusion made Kerala SIR credible | Onmanorama Explains
items.shows: It walks through Kerala's figures. The final roll is 8,97,211 below the 2024 roll (3.24 per cent), more than 98 per cent of the 36.89 lakh unmapped or discrepant electors were kept after hearings, and 92.7 per cent of 14.57 lakh Form 6 applications were accepted. Booth-level officers told the channel they were asked to include as many voters as possible.

items.title: Dhruv Rathee Interviews Former Chief Election Commissioner | Dr. S.Y. Quraishi
items.shows: A conversation in Hindi with S.Y. Quraishi, Chief Election Commissioner from 2010 to 2012. He says that after the revision of 2002 and 2003 the rolls were kept up to date by summary revision, with a booth level officer visiting each home and citizenship taken on the elector's own declaration in Form 6. He says almost every decision under the present Chief Election Commissioner is his alone, though the law asks for unanimity as far as possible and a majority otherwise. He argues that Form 6 cannot lawfully be used to bring back electors deleted in the revision, because it carries a declaration that the applicant has never been enrolled, and proposes a separate form approved by the Law Ministry. He also says the West Bengal election should be held again because it was held on a roll he regards as unlawful. He criticises the Supreme Court for letting that election go ahead and for sending judicial officers to do the Commission's work.

dropped.title: Election Commission Row: Is The SIR Process Legally Valid?
dropped.why: studio debate, owner's call to leave out. (oEmbed and watch-next confirm title, NDTV channel, 'Premiered Sep 25, 2026' and the description. The description names no participant and describes 'a heated legal debate' among senior advocates; it is discussion, not reporting.)
